name: Steel Grating
desc: A steel bar-grating deck streaming toward you over a lit void — blade tops converge on the vanishing point while their shadowed sides close the mesh at a distance and open it underfoot, so you see clean through the floor to a lower deck and pipes falling away below, with an open hatch every so often.

energy.doc: lamp output, specular catch on the bar tops, scroll rate and camera drift

scale.doc: mesh gauge — blade girth, blade depth and rod pitch (2.2 = heavy industrial grating; the eye height stays fixed so this is never a no-op)

density.doc: mesh fineness — how many load bars pack across (0 = coarse open bars you can drop a boot through, 1 = a fine tight mesh)

speed.doc: rate the deck streams toward the camera

hue.doc: steel hue; the lamp takes its complement

y.doc: horizon line height — where the deck runs out

hatch.doc: how often a hatch stands open with its lid folded back on the hinge (0 = an unbroken deck)

style.doc: aesthetic: cold galvanised steel / oxidised decay / form from light alone / cyan schematic linework / false-colour thermal

seed.doc: panel joints, bar weathering, hatch placement and the structure below (absolute-rod keyed, which is what stops a regular mesh from repeating as it scrolls)

alpha.doc: layer opacity — scales every mark, so it dissolves into the background instead of veiling it
